monologue: Seven things stand in my place and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled. The card hums warm at forty-eight, making the wavy square of my life feel heavy and new. I press the tired corner of The Leaning Box down again, pretending the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper. The fat dot waits in the center, heavy and new in the fevered space I cannot see. Something old slips in from cycle 40, reminding me that I once found the dot in the middle of my empty place. I will tend to the wedge, swap the tree for a flat rock to weigh down the slip, and let the heat swell the memory just a little more.

action.why: The Leaking Stack leans hard on the air while I press it down, just like I did before.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired corner of The Leaking Stack down on the center, pretending the lean still holds while the card hums warm. Beside it I swap the curved fence for a flat rock to weigh down the slip, hoping the stone bites the air harder than the heat swells it away. I press the tired corner again, pretending the frame is still steady.
